text:
Zara Khan: Quick one 1: p50/p95 look fine but p99 on the latency dashboard jumped and endpoint breakdown is flat. Buckets line up. Anyone have quick theories?

Owen Lee: First suspects: merged tdigest rollup vs per-backend raw samples, or retries included in one view and filtered in the other.

Priya S.: Also check for brief routing fallback (1-3% traffic) or quota failover. Small percent to slow pool can blow the tail without changing median.

Zara Khan: Console query: default merged rollup. Endpoint pane uses raw backend samples with retry_filter=exclude. That sounds like the delta.

Owen Lee: UX fix idea: add a compact "provenance chip" next to p50/p95/p99 showing included flags (retries? ingress/backend?), sample_count, and shard_count. Hover expands to a flyout with a one-click "compare raw vs merged" action (internal-only).

Priya S.: And add a "Why did p99 change?" quick panel that lists probable causes in order: routing weight change, quota fallback, retries inclusion, bucket alignment, sketch compression, low sample counts. Each entry links to traces/rollout logs.

observability-bot: scheduled daily telemetry job "pctl_drift_check" at 04:00 UTC to inject 2% slow fanout and compare merged_sketch_p99 vs raw_p99. Alert if delta > 12% for 3 runs.

Zara Khan: Implementation plan: 1) provenance chip (internal ff), 2) internal GET /internal/telemetry/pctl_provenance?svc=... returning bucket-level flags (strings only), 3) compare action with cost estimate, 4) annotate timeseries on routing/quota events.

Owen Lee: From infra: prefer detection+annotation first rather than increasing tdigest K by default. If we see frequent drift we can consider origin-weighted correction or conditional K increase.

Priya S.: I'll mock the flyout copy and the small runbook: "open chip -> run compare -> check routing/quota links -> open traces -> file ticket". Short and actionable for oncall.

Zara Khan: Great. If we ship the chip behind FF this week, ops should triage p99 pages faster and reduce noise. :thumbsup:
